title: Small-parcel spend audit + UPS/FedEx contract renegotiation on gain-share
product_service: Ingest a shipper's UPS/FedEx/regional-carrier invoice data, benchmark incentives/surcharges, renegotiate the carrier agreement, then audit invoices monthly (billing errors, address-correction/residential surcharges, duplicate charges, the few remaining guaranteed-service refunds). Fee = share of verified savings.
target_customer: Operations/finance lead at e-commerce brands, distributors and light manufacturers with roughly $250k-$5M/yr parcel spend (below the radar of the large negotiation consultancies' sweet spot).
purchase_motivation: Parcel is a top-3 cost line for shippers; annual carrier rate increases and surcharges compound; no-savings-no-fee lowers buyer risk.
spending_evidence: Parcel consultants widely charge only a percentage of savings generated [D, WS14-S020]; an operator since at least 2006 bills a share of actual monthly savings [D, WS14-S019]. Late-delivery refund pool has shrunk: UPS restored guarantees only for next-day air in 2021 [C, WS14-S016]; FedEx keeps most services suspended [A, WS14-S018]; ground services carry no guarantee as of late 2026 [D, WS14-S017].
representative_operators: Refund Retriever, LLC - parcel audit & negotiation since >=2006, fee = share of monthly savings; size unknown [D, WS14-S019]
TransImpact - parcel negotiation/analytics firm marketing percentage-of-savings model [D, WS14-S020]
revenue_mechanism: Percentage of realized savings vs. a contractually defined baseline for the term of the carrier agreement (typically 1-3 yrs), plus % of audit refunds. Exact market fee % MISSING (analyst expectation 25-50% of savings) [E].
typical_transaction_value: Illustrative: $1M/yr parcel spend x 10-20% savings = $100-200k/yr; at an assumed 30% share = $30-60k/yr per client for 2-3 yrs [E].
direct_costs: Analyst time for data normalization and monthly audit; rate-modeling software/data; sales commissions.
contribution_profit_note: Per client perhaps $20-45k/yr contribution after analyst time at assumed fee levels [E].
working_capital_note: No inventory. Savings realized only after new agreement goes live (6-8 week negotiation per WS14-S019) and fees billed monthly/quarterly in arrears; 3-5 months of founder time unpaid before first fee.
sales_cycle: 1-4 months: free benchmark analysis -> signed savings-share agreement -> carrier negotiation (6-8 weeks).
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract: savings share over agreement term; renegotiation every 2-3 yrs; ongoing monthly audit.
acquisition_channels: Outbound to e-commerce ops/finance (Shopify/Amazon brand lists, Inc. 5000 lists)
Partnerships with fractional CFOs/bookkeepers and e-commerce agencies
Content: carrier-surcharge teardown posts and free savings calculators
customer_accessibility: Many identifiable shippers; decision-makers reachable by outbound. Credibility wall: buyers are pitched constantly by parcel consultants and must share invoice data.
supplier_accessibility: N/A (no suppliers); carrier account reps must accept negotiation - some carriers push back on third-party consultants [E].
competitive_intensity: high - many parcel consultancies, SaaS audit tools, 3PLs offering pooled rates, carriers' own reps.
entry_strategy: Focus on the $250k-$3M shipper segment with a fast, free, data-driven benchmark and month-to-month audit; specialize in one vertical (e.g., supplements, auto parts) to build benchmark depth.
licenses: None specific; general business registration. Not freight brokerage (no FMCSA authority needed because no transportation is arranged) [E].
regulatory_barriers: Low. Carrier agreements may contain confidentiality clauses restricting disclosure of pricing to third parties [E].
operational_risks: Thin benchmark data vs. incumbents with thousands of agreements; baseline/attribution disputes; data access depends on client exporting carrier billing files.
financial_risks: Clients churn after first renegotiation or migrate to 3PL pooled rates; shipping volume declines cut fees.
founder_expertise: Carrier pricing mechanics (zones, DIM, incentive tiers, accessorials, surcharges), contract structures, negotiation tactics; data analysis fits founder background.
staffing: Founder solo for first ~8-10 clients; then pricing analyst(s) and one sales/BDR.
automation_potential: High: invoice parsing, surcharge anomaly detection, rate modeling, benchmark scenarios can be software/AI-driven at ordinary cost. Negotiation, trust-building and carrier relationship stay human.
delegation_potential: Analysts can run audits with SOPs; negotiation delegable after 2-3 yrs of playbook building.
scalability: National market, but scale limited by sales capacity and benchmark depth; a $1-3M revenue boutique is plausible.
expansion: LTL/TL freight audit (WS14-002), regional-carrier rate brokering, packaging/DIM optimization consulting, 3PL selection advisory.
roic_note: Capital at risk is mostly founder time plus <$12k; ROIC very high if 10+ clients are signed, near zero if not.
critical_assumptions: Sub-$3M shippers still achieve 10-20% savings from renegotiation
A 25-50% savings share is accepted by this segment
Carriers negotiate with third-party-advised shippers
unanswered_questions: Published fee % benchmarks for parcel negotiation consultants
Carrier policies toward consultants and confidentiality clauses
Share of SMB shippers already on 3PL/aggregator rates
Typical client retention after first agreement
failure_modes: Cannot beat incumbents' benchmark data, so savings are small
Clients take the new agreement and terminate before savings share accrues
score_rationale: fcf 4: boutique economics, fee % unverified. roic 8: near-zero capital. access 5: reachable but crowded inbox. entry 4: crowded, wedge is segment focus. ai 7: invoice analytics genuinely cheaper with software.
preliminary_verdict: advance - asset-light recurring savings-share model that fits a data-oriented founder; validate fee levels and SMB savings depth first.

title: LTL/truckload freight bill audit, overcharge and cargo-claim recovery for mid-market shippers
product_service: Pre- or post-payment audit of LTL/TL freight invoices (rate vs. tariff/contract, freight class/density reclassification, reweigh, accessorials, duplicates), filing overcharge claims and cargo loss/damage claims with carriers; optional freight-payment processing.
target_customer: Controllers/logistics managers at manufacturers and distributors with ~$1-20M/yr LTL/TL spend and no TMS-based audit.
purchase_motivation: Billing errors are routine in LTL (reweigh/reclass); finance teams lack time to audit; recovered cash is found money.
spending_evidence: Freight audit & pay firms charge 15-25% of recovered savings or a flat per-invoice fee; unaudited programs lose 3-5% of freight spend to billing errors; LTL reweigh/reclass variances 5-25% per shipment [D, WS14-S021]. Incumbent claims 20% invoice error rate and up to 8% recovered savings [D, WS14-S022].
representative_operators: AFS Logistics - freight audit/payment incumbent [D, WS14-S022]
Nuvocargo - carrier publishing audit-fee benchmarks (not an auditor) [D, WS14-S021]
revenue_mechanism: 15-25% contingency on recoveries [D, WS14-S021] or per-invoice audit fee; optional payment-processing float/fee.
typical_transaction_value: Illustrative: $5M freight spend x 3-5% errors [D] = $150-250k recoverable x 20% = $30-50k/yr per client [E, derived].
direct_costs: Audit analysts, rating-engine/tariff data subscriptions, claim-filing labor.
working_capital_note: Contingency fees paid after carriers credit/refund (30-120 days); payment-processing variant requires funding float and bonding - avoid early.
sales_cycle: 1-3 months; free retrospective audit of a sample of past invoices as door-opener.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract: ongoing monthly audit once embedded in AP workflow.
acquisition_channels: Outbound to controllers at manufacturers/distributors (industrial directories)
Partnerships with freight brokers/TMS vendors who don't audit
customer_accessibility: Identifiable buyers; moderate cycle; need access to freight invoices and carrier contracts/tariffs.
supplier_accessibility: Tariff/rating data (e.g., carrier base rates) assumed licensable; access terms unknown.
competitive_intensity: high - established audit & pay firms, TMS vendors with built-in audit, brokers bundling audit.
entry_strategy: Target shippers below $3M spend that incumbents deprioritize; combine LTL audit with parcel (WS14-001) into one 'transportation cost recovery' offer.
licenses: None for audit; freight payment services may face money-transmitter questions if handling client funds [E].
regulatory_barriers: Low; carrier claim time limits (overcharge/cargo claim filing windows) govern recoverability [E].
operational_risks: Classification rule changes and carrier dispute processes are labor-intensive; poor data quality from clients.
financial_risks: Recoveries shrink as client fixes root causes; fee disputes on 'found' errors.
founder_expertise: LTL pricing (classification/density, tariffs, accessorials), claims law basics (Carmack liability), audit tooling.
automation_potential: High: OCR/AI invoice extraction, BOL vs invoice matching, re-rating against contracts; human handles carrier disputes.
scalability: National; scale tied to analyst capacity and sales.
expansion: Parcel (WS14-001), freight procurement bids, claims-only service, payment processing later.
roic_note: Low capital; returns driven by client count; ROIC high if sales succeed.
critical_assumptions: Mid-market shippers without TMS audit still lose 3-5% to errors
15-25% contingency fee holds for small clients
Rating data can be obtained affordably
unanswered_questions: Share of mid-market shippers already using audit services
Effect of recent freight-classification changes on error rates
failure_modes: Recoveries too small per client to cover analyst labor
score_rationale: fcf 4: modest per-client fees. access 4: needs invoice data and trust from controllers. entry 4: crowded. ai 7: extraction/re-rating is where AI cuts labor.
preliminary_verdict: advance - pair with WS14-001 as a single transportation-cost-recovery firm; validate error rates on sample data.

Competitive density among telecom agents doing free audits

title: Sales/use tax reverse audit (overpayment recovery) for manufacturers and other heavy purchasers
product_service: Review purchase invoices, fixed-asset ledgers, utility bills and use-tax accruals to find tax paid on exempt items (e.g., manufacturing machinery & equipment, production inputs, resale, out-of-state deliveries), then prepare refund/credit claims (or vendor refund requests) with documentation; fee from recovered tax.
target_customer: CFO/controller at manufacturers, printers, distributors and other companies with >$10M/yr taxable purchases, starting in Illinois and neighboring states.
purchase_motivation: Cash refunds with no upfront cost; vendors routinely over-collect on exempt purchases.
spending_evidence: CPA firms market reverse audits to manufacturers and claim manufacturers average $75k+/yr in overpaid sales/use tax [D, WS14-S009]; contingent fees on net tax recovered are common [C, WS14-S010]; findings-based fees restricted in some jurisdictions and for public companies [D, WS14-S029].
representative_operators: Cherry Bekaert - CPA firm reverse-audit practice [D, WS14-S009]
CliftonLarsonAllen - reverse audits/utility refund studies [D, WS14-S029]
Big-4 and regional CPA SALT practices (KPMG, Andersen) - incumbents, fees unknown [D]
revenue_mechanism: Contingency % of net tax refunded/credited (market % MISSING; analyst expectation 20-40%) [E]; some hourly/flat hybrids [C, WS14-S010].
typical_transaction_value: Illustrative: $75k/yr overpaid [D] x ~3-yr lookback = ~$225k refund x 25% = ~$56k one-time fee per client [E].
direct_costs: Analyst/reviewer time, document retrieval, occasional tax-attorney review for contested claims.
working_capital_note: Long cash lag: fee earned only when IDOR/vendor pays or credits (often 6-18 months) [E]; requires funding 6-12 months of operations.
sales_cycle: 2-6 months; requires NDA and access to AP/ERP data.
repeat_purchase: occasional: lookback once, then periodic re-reviews every 2-3 yrs; can convert to ongoing exemption-certificate/accrual monitoring retainer.
acquisition_channels: Outbound to manufacturer CFOs (Illinois Manufacturers' Association directories)
Partnerships with small CPA firms lacking SALT depth
customer_accessibility: Buyers identifiable; credibility wall vs. CPA firms; data access is the hurdle.
competitive_intensity: moderate - CPA SALT practices and specialist recovery firms, but mid-market manufacturers are under-served [E].
entry_strategy: Specialize in one exemption cluster (e.g., Illinois manufacturing M&E and production-related purchases) and offer no-cost assessment; partner with small CPA firms that refer and review.
licenses: No license needed to prepare claims: Illinois IL-2848 accepts a non-attorney/non-CPA 'other' POA (with witness/notary step), but an attorney must represent in IDOR administrative hearings or the Independent Tax Tribunal [A, WS14-S008]. Other states' rules vary.
regulatory_barriers: Contingent-fee restrictions in some jurisdictions/for public companies [D, WS14-S029]; claim statutes of limitation (Illinois lookback length to verify) [E]; vendor-refund route needed where tax was paid to vendors [E].
operational_risks: Technical errors in exemption interpretation lead to denied claims or audit exposure for client; contested claims need attorneys.
financial_risks: Long payout lag; claims denied after work done; concentration in few large wins.
geographic_constraints: Start Illinois/Midwest; multi-state possible with state-specific knowledge.
founder_expertise: Illinois ROT/use tax exemptions, claim procedures, audit evidence standards - 3-6 months of study plus mentorship.
staffing: Reviewer analysts (ex-AP/tax staff) after first wins; contract tax attorney for disputes.
automation_potential: High: AI extraction/classification of invoice line items against exemption rules; humans validate and argue claims.
delegation_potential: Analyst-delegable with SOPs; tax judgment stays with senior reviewer.
scalability: Regional to national with state modules; reinvestment in analysts.
expansion: Use-tax compliance monitoring retainer, utility-tax refund studies, other states, property-tax (where non-attorney allowed).
roic_note: Capital is working capital for a 6-12 month cash lag (~$20-60k incl. founder runway); payoffs large per engagement.
critical_assumptions: Mid-market Illinois manufacturers have material overpayments not already recovered
Illinois lookback and claim procedures allow recovery of 2-3+ years
Clients accept ~25% contingency from a non-CPA firm
unanswered_questions: Illinois claim-for-credit limitation period and purchaser vs. vendor refund mechanics
Whether non-CPA firms face reputational barriers with CFOs
failure_modes: Long payout lag starves the firm
Technical mistakes cause denials or client audits
CPA firms bundle reverse audits into existing relationships
score_rationale: fcf 5: large per-engagement fees plausible but unverified. cash 3: 6-18 month lag. feasibility 7: no license, attorney needed only for hearings [A]. ai 7: line-item classification is AI-friendly.
preliminary_verdict: advance - legally open to a non-CPA in Illinois with high-ticket contingency fees; the cash lag and technical-credibility hurdle need validation.

title: Cook County / Illinois property-tax appeal service (contingency on tax savings)
product_service: Evidence packages (comparables, valuation, vacancy/income data) and appeal filings at the Assessor, Board of Review and PTAB; fee = share of first-year tax savings.
target_customer: Owners of commercial, industrial and multifamily property (mostly entities) and homeowners in Cook and collar counties.
purchase_motivation: Property tax is the largest operating cost for many owners; Cook County reassessment cycles create recurring appeal windows.
spending_evidence: Ownwell reportedly charges 25% of savings in Illinois [D, WS14-S006]; competitor claims 62% Cook County appeal success [D, WS14-S007].
representative_operators: Ownwell - tech-enabled appeal service, ~25% contingency in IL per third-party review [D, WS14-S006]
Cook County property-tax law firms (many, contingency-based) [D, WS14-S007]
revenue_mechanism: Contingency % of tax savings (~25% residential per WS14-S006; attorney firms 25-40% per search summary) [D].
direct_costs: Data/comps, analyst time, attorney time (mandatory for entity-owned property at the Board of Review).
contribution_profit_note: Only meaningful if structured as/with a law firm [E].
working_capital_note: Fee paid after tax bill reflects reduction - often 6-12+ months [E].
sales_cycle: Seasonal by township reassessment calendar; 30-day filing windows after notices.
customer_accessibility: Owners identifiable from public assessor data; high buyer awareness.
competitive_intensity: extreme - entrenched Cook County tax-appeal law firms plus Ownwell-type platforms.
entry_strategy: No legal wedge: only licensed attorneys may practice before the Board of Review and corporation-owned property must use a lawyer [A, WS14-S001]; at the Assessor stage no party must use an attorney [A, WS14-S002] but representation of others by non-attorneys is unverified; a pending bill (HB4931) would allow non-attorney representatives for entities [A, WS14-S003].
licenses: Illinois law license required for Board of Review practice and entity representation [A, WS14-S001]; a non-lawyer cannot share legal fees with lawyers (IL Rules of Professional Conduct 5.4, analyst knowledge) [E].
regulatory_barriers: Unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure; fee-splitting and paid-referral restrictions on attorneys [E].
financial_risks: Long fee lag; contingent on outcomes.
geographic_constraints: County-specific rules; downstate PTAB representation rules unverified (ilga.gov unavailable).
founder_expertise: Mass appraisal, comps, Cook County calendars; but legally needs a JD.
automation_potential: Comps/valuation automation is strong (Ownwell's model), but legal gate dominates.
scalability: Large market, legally closed to this founder in its most valuable segment.
expansion: Data/analytics vendor to tax-appeal law firms on flat SaaS fees (not referral fees); revisit if HB4931 or similar passes.
roic_note: Low capital but legal gate blocks the profitable segment.
critical_assumptions: Board of Review attorney-only rule remains in force
Non-attorney residential representation at CCAO is legally unclear
unanswered_questions: Whether paid non-attorney agents may file for individual homeowners at CCAO and PTAB
How Ownwell structures Cook County filings (attorney partner?)
failure_modes: Inability to monetize via attorney partners due to fee-sharing bans
score_rationale: feasibility 2: attorney-only at Board of Review and for corporate owners [A]. entry 3: entrenched law firms. Evidence A on the legal gate.
gates: G2_LICENSE:FAIL (Cook County Board of Review practice and entity-owned property require an Illinois attorney; fee-splitting with lawyers barred)
preliminary_verdict: reject - the valuable segment legally requires an attorney; monitor HB4931 and consider a flat-fee analytics product for law firms only as a minor adjacency.

title: Unclaimed property & surplus-funds locator (finder) service
product_service: Identify businesses and individuals (or heirs) with sizable unclaimed property held by state treasuries (and surplus funds from foreclosure/tax sales), locate them, and file claims under a fee agreement.
target_customer: Businesses with unclaimed vendor credits/refunds; estates/heirs; individuals with large holdings.
purchase_motivation: Found money with no effort; owners unaware property exists.
spending_evidence: Illinois caps finder fees at 10% of amount collected and requires a Treasurer-issued finder license, fidelity bond (up to $100k) and $500 application fee; a waiting period applies [A, WS14-S004, WS14-S005].
representative_operators: Licensed Illinois finders (roster not reviewed) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Contingency fee capped at 10% in Illinois [A, WS14-S004]; other states' caps vary (unverified) [E].
typical_transaction_value: Illinois: 10% of claims; a $20k claim yields $2k [E derived from A cap].
direct_costs: Skip-tracing data, outreach (mail/phone), claim paperwork, bond premium.
contribution_profit_note: Thin in Illinois at a 10% cap given outreach costs and conversion [E].
working_capital_note: Paid when the state pays claimant (months); bond premium upfront.
sales_cycle: Weeks per claimant; trust barrier high (looks like a scam to owners).
customer_accessibility: Owners identifiable from public lists but highly skeptical; states push free self-claim.
competitive_intensity: moderate - established finders; state outreach campaigns make free claiming easy.
entry_strategy: Focus on large business claims in states with higher caps; B2B unclaimed-property recovery for companies' own funds.
licenses: Illinois finder license from the State Treasurer, fidelity bond, background check [A, WS14-S004].
regulatory_barriers: 10% fee cap and waiting period in Illinois [A, WS14-S004, WS14-S005]; other states have their own caps/registrations [E].
operational_risks: Low conversion; reputational association with scams.
founder_expertise: Skip tracing, state claim procedures, probate basics.
automation_potential: Matching public lists to high-value owners is automatable; outreach trust is human.
expansion: Business-side unclaimed-property compliance (escheat reporting) - overlaps WS12/WS15.
roic_note: Low capital; low returns at a 10% cap.
critical_assumptions: Enough high-value claims exist that owners haven't claimed
Other states permit higher fees
unanswered_questions: Illinois surplus-funds rules after Tyler v. Hennepin (2023)
score_rationale: fcf 2: 10% cap [A] plus outreach costs. feasibility 6: license+bond obtainable. scale 3: state-by-state.
preliminary_verdict: reject - Illinois' 10% cap and licensing make the economics thin; at most a multi-state niche.
